newsitem.title: USA: Harley-Davidson and Porsche form joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Harley-Davidson and Porsche form joint venture.

text.p: Harley-Davidson Motor Co. and German sports car maker Dr. Ing. h.c.F. Porsche AG said Wednesday they have formed a joint venture to buy and assemble engines and transmission systems for use in new motorcycles and components.
The venture extends a relationship since the 1970s between the only major U.S.-based motorcycle manufacturer and the world's largest manufacturer of sports cars.
The joint venture plans to operate out of one of Harley-Davidson's U.S. manufacturing facilities.

Each party will invest less than $10 million over the life of the joint venture, which will last about five years from the time it begins production. However, they said production will not begin until "years in the future."

"Harley-Davidson will invest less than $10 million in the venture over several years, but will invest approximately $200 million in capital expenditures in 1997 alone," the Milwaukee-based company said.
Harley-Davidson sold 118,771 motorcycles in 1996 and earned $166 million on net sales of $1.5 billion.
Its stock rose 25 cents to $47.25 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly after midday.
